blocks.x: Welcome to Timor-Leste, officially one of Asia’s least visited countries, where we are hunting down the ultimate $1 spicy street food! Unless you've traveled to this hidden Southeast Asian nation, you've probably never experienced Timorese food culture before—and honestly, I had no clue what to expect.

Just an hour after landing in the capital city of Dili, I met up with local chef and entrepreneur Cesar Gaio (https://www.instagram.com/cesar_gaio/) to discover exactly what locals love to eat. We are unlocking a vibrant culinary scene that has practically never been seen on camera!

From active street food markets packed with cheap, fiery dishes to a 40-minute drive out of town for fresh beachside seafood, this country completely blew me away. We also dive into the unique fusion history of Dili, tasting incredible Timorese-Chinese dishes at Linivon Restaurant and wrapping things up with legendary Indonesian flavors at Martabak Mas Boy.

🎬 What’s In This Video
Dili Street Food Market: Meeting up with Cesar Gaio and diving straight into the action with an incredible variety of cheap, spicy local street food.
Beachside Seafood & Road Trip: Escaping the capital for a quick drive to a stunning beach to eat fresh local seafood right on the coast (plus a quick palm fruit snack on the way back!).
Timorese Chinese Cuisine: Tasting the historical culinary crossover at Linivon Restaurant.
Food Court Indonesian Fusion: Heading to a hidden food court to try iconic Indonesian-style dishes at Martabak Mas Boy.
